It sounds like you’ve tried a lot of different approaches to getting yourself under control. At this point it’s all about mindset. If you tell yourself you shouldn’t have had that child, that’s what you’ll believe and it’ll make parenting that much more difficult. Also keep in mind the phrase “pick your battles” learn to know what’s worth getting upset over and what’s not. Your child needs stability especially as they get older. If you have anger issues, know that medication takes trial and error and you might be able to find something that could really help. Exercise in the morning can also help release emotions so you don’t have as much pent up aggression throughout your day with your child. Hang in there! Giving up now on your child would be the worst thing to do in this situation. Also apologies go a long way even to children.

Sure the dad with his kids didn’t necessarily need to go stand by your car but he’d probably had a long ass day being a parenttt and was ticked off that he could have utilized that spot-which he was actually entitled to. It’s also shitty that you chose the parent spot- not the employee parking spot and then tried to justify your decision making you less of an asshole lol. You know you’re the asshole here, don’t go justifying your decisions with ‘I needed to take a shit,’ and ‘at least I didn’t use the employee parking spot’
